title: Fivetran Sync Latency and Lag
dataSources: Fivetran log-service events and REST API (`connectors`, sync status), Airbyte job logs (`airbyte:job`), Matillion task history, Kafka Connect connector/task status, AWS Glue job runs (CloudWatch), ADF pipeline runs (Azure Monitor).
app: Fivetran / Airbyte / Stitch / Matillion logs and REST APIs via HEC scripted inputs; Kafka Connect JMX/REST; cloud ELT via `Splunk_TA_aws` (Glue) and `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (ADF).
spl:
index=dataops sourcetype=fivetran:log event=sync_end status=SUCCESS
| eval lag_min=round(sync_duration/60,1)
| stats avg(lag_min) as avg_min, p95(lag_min) as p95_min, latest(_time) as last_sync by connector_name
| eval mins_since=round((now()-last_sync)/60,0)
| where p95_min>60 OR mins_since>180
| sort - mins_since
description: Measures Fivetran sync duration and time since last successful sync, flagging connectors whose data is lagging behind its expected freshness.
value: Even successful connectors can fall behind schedule; lag tracking catches data that is quietly getting stale before users notice.
implementation: Ingest sync events; schedule hourly; tune thresholds to each connector's sync frequency; alert on excessive lag.
visualization: Table by lag/last-sync, timechart of sync latency.
grandmaExplanation: We measure how fresh each incoming data feed is so you know when one is falling behind, even if it has not failed.
